statement.p: Compute the flux of \vec F=x\vec i+y\vec j+z\vec k through the curved surface of the cylinder x^2+y^2=1 bounded below by the plane x+y+z=3, above by the plane x+y+z=8, and oriented away from the z-axis.

static.solution:
\vec r=x\vec i+y\vec j+z\vec k =\cos t\vec i+ \sin t\vec j + s \vec k, where 0\leq t\leq 2\pi and 3- \cos t- \sin t\leq s\leq 8 - \cos t - \sin t.
The vector \partial \vec r/\partial t\times\partial\vec r/\partial s points away from the z-axis, so d\vec A=\left({\partial\vec r}/{\partial t}\times {\partial\vec r}/{\partial s}\right)\,ds\, dt and \vec F\cdot d\vec A = \left|\begin{array}{ccc} x \amp y \amp z\\ -\sin t \amp \cos t \amp 0\\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1\end{array}\right| \,ds\,dt = ( x\cos t + y\sin t)\,ds\,dt. Plugging in for x and y, this is \vec F\cdot d\vec A = (\cos^2 t+\sin^2 t)\,ds\,dt = \, ds\,dt. Hence, \int_S\vec F\cdot d\vec A = \int_0^{2\pi}\int_{3-\cos t-\sin t}^{8-\cos t-\sin t} \,ds\, dt = \int_0^{2\pi} 5\,dt = 10\pi.
